Certain parties suggest that the formula distances be measured from a central point in the base municipality rather than from its corporate limits. The attraction of such an approach is apparent. By swinging an arc about the city utilizing a radius measured from the city center, the limits of a particular commercial zone could be easily delineated without reference to the vagaries of corporate limits. The difficulty in implementing this suggestion is that there is no commonly accepted fixed central point in most cities from which to measure the relevant mileage Consequently, we believe that the adoption of radius. this alternative would lead to significant interpretational and administrative problems. Corporate limits at least provide an established and generally known line from which to measure the formula distance. Furthermore, many cities along lakes, rivers, or other natural barriers are extremely elongated in shape. Circular zone limits measured by a single radius from the center of such a city would quite likely yield unsatisfactory results. Differing topographic characteristics of individual cities are better captured through measurement of the formula distance from corporate limits.

While this suggestion has a theoretical appeal, we abide by our previous decision that implementation of this approach is not administratively feasible for the reasons stated in the Interim Report, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 166 and 209-10.
